items.note: S1.1 names the copy/gather/scatter/side-injection gates, the forward-backward-forward stages, the bank exchange and the restoration of arbitrary scratch values, but gives the result only as an exchange 'up to a sign' rather than (X_a,Y_a) to (-Y_a,X_a). It also omits the per-invocation effect y_S <- y_S + x_S, the triple indexing with h=100 and the neighbour rules. It is a single infer step with no derivation of the net map (JV+RG)x.

The common frame commuting with a pointwise linear gate is stated correctly. The conclusion is given as 'only the endpoint operator D_out D_in^{-1} remains', which drops the scalar network S_Omega and the route sign epsilon_w of D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}. It also never says that an edge applies D_v D_u^{-1}.

The bit-network budget is correct and its counting follows the paper: the triple-indicator form, the telescoping to Wm-2N, only centre 3->4 edges decreasing (by h each), L=Ich, the sum Wm-2N+2L, and L_b/N=100/539. The complex ratio 101/539 and the binary orthonormal-basis claim are missing. The essential construction is never shown: the terminal labels, the stage transitions and the gate-label table, and the residual check that every edge is comparable and that only centre 3->4 decreases. All of it is taken from one quoted line (999).

The rank sum is derived as in the paper (rank P_V-P_U = dim V - dim U, with N exceptional source edges of rank one), giving s_b=W_bm-N+2L_b<W_bm. The vertex matrices are described loosely as 'P_U at vertices': the -P_{U_a} source assignment appears only through the 'negative source projections'. The endpoint identity M_sink(rho(w))-M_source(w)=I_m appears only as an input to S1.5.3. Its proof, P_{U_a^perp}+P_{U_a}=I with zero source and identity sink elsewhere, is never given.

S2.1 correctly states one translation kernel aI+bX_v per orthonormal residual vector and C^{tensor m} on every role after corrections. It does not define the phase frames C_U=H^{tensor m} diag(i^{q_U}) H^{tensor m}, and it gives only s<Wm instead of s_c=W_cm-2N+2L_c. It is a bare infer step with no derivation (weight additivity mod 4, the Z-corrections on the 27 support coordinates).

For the bit network the chain L_b/N<1/2 -> deficit N-2L_b>0 -> relative deficit >20*2^{-50} with log m<20 -> s/W<m^tau, tau=1-2^{-50} follows the paper. The exact deficits eta_b and eta_c are absent, as is the inequality m^{1-2^{-50}}>m(1-20*2^{-50}) itself. The complex half is also absent: s_c<W_cm with deficit 2N-2L_c, and sigma=tau. sigma appears only as a bound in S2.6.3.

The plan refers to the single-digit elementary operation in O(V) and to linear-time controlled updates of a later field from earlier ones. It never states either lemma's content: the list of digit operations and row splits, or the y <- y+a(controls) mod q^b update with its b^{O(1)} offset condition.

Both the factorization A=E_1 Pi E_2 and the cost (exactly a interchanges plus O(V)) are stated correctly, although the setting over Z/q^b with a fixed odd prime q is left implicit. The application of the factors and the one-interchange implementation of each pivot follow the paper (lines 1432-1443). The elimination proof of the factorization is missing, and so is the choice of q avoiding all denominators.

Every step of the proof is reproduced in order: the k=0 case, the cyclic row split into W streams of volume V/W, the edge shears done by recursive interchanges, the endpoint identity giving H<-H+D, the three-update interchange, s calls, the recurrence and its geometric sum, and the depth-first fixed-tape schedule. S1.5's statement omits the hypothesis that a row field preceding both chunks has length divisible by W^k.

The steps follow the proof: high digits as rows (rho=O(log e)), padding to R'<2R, the base-m decomposition with a_j<m, the geometric sum O(Ve^tau), and padding from binary to radix-q ranges. The field-order shuffling of the high digits is compressed to 'moved separately', which does not hide an essential step.

The steps state that basis changes reduce to a fixed number of packed row additions, that there are exactly s child calls on f=e/m axes with no extra calls from inverse wrappers, and that H_0^{tensor D}=b^D S_D C^{tensor D} S_D. The central mechanism is missing: conjugation by P_M turns the directional kernels C_{v_j} into coordinate kernels C_{e_j}. The inverse-child identity (C^{-1})^{tensor f}=(-i)^f Z C Z is only alluded to.

The operation at j_i=rho+iK, the bad fraction 80(f-1)2^{-K} and the time bound are correct, and the route (eight rotations, then an exact sorting repair) is the paper's. Several essential steps are missing: why the eight lines flip u's parity and restore the auxiliary chunk z, the guard interval with its union bound, the fact that T_0 S_0^{-1} permutes only the bad set, the chunk swaps that position the target, and the separate last position j_{f-1}.

The recurrence F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1) with leaves O(e), the bound O(e^lambda) on internal costs, the leaf bound and the base-m partition into O(d^{lambda'}) all match the paper. The plan never says where the rows come from: the first q_0=O(log d) chunks as row index, padded to a multiple of W^{k_0}. It also does not derive the node overhead from the packed lemma.

The statement is correct: the H_0 layer on D<=d chunks in O(Vd^{lambda'}), exact evaluation with p+ceil(C_0 d^{C_1}) fractional bits (O(p) width), and one truncation with error below sqrt2 2^{-p}. The route is the paper's, but the guard-width argument is only asserted in S2.7. The depth recurrence A(e)<=sA(e/m)+E, the bound E=64(W+m+1)^3 and the magnitude/denominator induction are not given.

The steps follow the paper for character cancellation, the decimation-in-frequency step, bit-reversed storage (B_tF_t^-, F_t^+B_t^{-1}), grouped rounds with monomial twiddles, and the three-part layout cost with error sqrt2 l 2^{-p}. The exact counterparts LBF_t^- and F_t^+B^{-1}L^{-1} of the laid-out procedures are never stated or derived. The per-round single-truncation argument (J_E Q_p = Q_p J_E) is also missing. S3.1.1 has the sign of omega reversed.

The steps reproduce the proof: B_0=2^{4p}, A_u=u(B_0) in 4pr bits, the separation |h_j|<B_0/2, two's-complement packing with carries in {-1,0}, centred extraction with carries in {0,1}, and four dominating integer products with wrapping mod y^r+1.

Error, cost, procedure (two forwards kept in LB order, pointwise products, opposite transform, exact scale by M), normalization identity, commutation of a record permutation with pointwise products, and the 3delta+eta error bound all match the paper.

The identity P_sF_s=2^{2alpha^2}B_0P_tF_tA is derived along the paper's route: the Gaussian identity, the Neumann inversion of N=CTD, and renormalized contractions. The tensor form with gamma=2d alpha^2 and the exposure cost are stated. Missing are the hypothesis theta>p/alpha^4, the definitions of P_s and P_t, and the approximation guarantees (error <p^2, time O(tp^{3/2+delta}alpha) per line). The ordered selection C and the linewise padded-box implementation are not covered either.

Both identities are stated exactly and derived as in the paper: the periodicity of the chirp, the coefficient computation for QF_t, the substitution h=ck giving RF_s^+R=F_s^+, and the two normalizations. The remark that conjugation yields RF_s^+ is not in this subtree.

The exponents, sizes, Theta relations, alpha and gamma, and the prime interval with T/2<S<T are all correct. delta=1/16, beta=1/2, C_1=20 and eta=1/(4d) are omitted. The verifications are only asserted: the layer inequalities, the Bernoulli bound (1-1/2d)^d>1/2, alpha^4 theta_i>3db>=p, and the n^{o(1)} prime search.

The steps reproduce the paper's argument: the map x -> prod x_i^{mu_i} with mu_i=P_i^{-1} mod s_i, the isomorphism argument, the triangular coordinate formula, the prefix-controlled cyclic shifts preserving zero padding, and the axis reversal by O(d^2) moves at cost O(Tpd^2(1+l^tau)).

The exact isomorphism x_d -> zeta y, its diagonal isometric form and the wrap check zeta^{k+l}(-1)^h=zeta^j are given as in the paper. The interface formula M_C(f,g)=D_- iota^{-1} M_r(iota D_+ f, iota D_+ g)=(f*g)/T is not given. The computed twisted convolution, with its twist errors below 4*2^{-p}, is also not covered.

The source-transform composition with exact counterpart RF_s and the six algorithm steps with their scales match the paper. The normalization bookkeeping (u*v)/S^2 -> (u*v)/S -> integer convolution is also correct in S8.8. The opposite procedure F~^+(z)=conj(F~(conj z)) is never defined, and the S8 method misattributes the digit-scale undo to the second S.

E_ring=M(3L+2)<5TL, E_s=9*2^gamma TL, the cancellation G(U.V_1)=(u*v)/S^2, E_w<28*2^gamma T^2 L, the final bound below 1/2, rounding and carries all match the paper. The chain skips the complex-convolution (<6TL) and chirp (<8TL) error steps and the disk margins (.7, .6, .51). Those are what make E_s follow.

The conclusion is correct: min margin g_2=epsilon c(1-tau)=2^{-181}=2kappa, giving O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}) with schoolbook below a cutoff. Only three of the seven table rows are tabulated (dK, pK^{tau-1}, l d^{lambda'}). The CRT, Gaussian, chirp and packed-product rows are left to other subtrees and are not converted to powers of p. The o(V) bounds for setup and exceptional-stream sorting are absent.

S0 says the bound disproves the n log n optimality conjecture in this model. It never gives the content: an eventual lower bound c_A n lg n for every machine, refuted by one machine with liminf T_A(n)/(n lg n)=0.

errors.says: Along a route only the endpoint operator D_out D_in^{-1} remains.
errors.paper: The implemented operator is D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}. A route w -> rho(w) applies epsilon_w D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1}, so the scalar routing and its sign remain.

errors.says: The transforms F_t^{+-} average t copies of the input weighted by powers of omega_t^{-+1}.
errors.paper: (F_t^- z)_j uses omega_t^{-jk} and (F_t^+ z)_j uses omega_t^{jk}, so F_t^{+-} is weighted by powers of omega_t^{+-1}; the plan's sign is reversed.

errors.says: Method: move the top bits of each axis to a prefix with bit moves.
errors.paper: The prefix receives the top slot (i,l-1) only of the length-2^l axes, followed by the low b=(l-1) mod K slots of every axis. S3.2.2 states this correctly.

errors.says: Method: one scale by S undoes the transform normalization and the second undoes the digit scaling.
errors.paper: Both factors S undo the 1/S^2 normalization: the first gives w=(u*v)/S and the second removes the remaining 1/S. The factor 2^{2b+4} reverses the two input digit scales.

chain: The S1 subtree follows the paper's route from the scratch-restoring exchange through frames, labels, the rank budget s_b<W_bm, the matrix shear and the power-width recurrence to O(Vu^tau). S2-S10 assemble the layer, transforms, resampling, recovery and cost table in the paper's order and reach O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}). The tree thins where results are only quoted rather than derived: the label construction behind 'only centre 3->4 edges decrease', the endpoint identity, the whole complex phase interface and P_M conjugation, the guard-width depth bound, the chirp error steps, and four of the seven cost-table rows.

steps.note: The scratch-restoring bank exchange is described by gate types and three stages. The plan never gives h=100, the data pairs indexed by triples with N=binom(h,3)^3 and m=h^3, or the exact map (X_a,Y_a) -> (-Y_a,X_a): it says only 'up to a sign'.

S1.2 carries the mechanism: arrays stored in frames D_v, and a pointwise linear gate commuting with its common frame, so only the endpoint frames matter on a route. S1.3's motivation makes the edge cost a change of frame. It loosely writes D_out D_in^{-1} without S_Omega.

The labels are subspaces of a fixed m-dimensional space built from tensor products of triple indicators, with nondegenerate and orthogonal neighbouring lines and nested labels on edges. The only decreasing edges are centre 3->4, each losing h.
For U subset V, P_V-P_U has rank dim V - dim U. The N negative source projections are the exceptions, each first edge matrix 2P_{U_a} having rank one.
The budget sum |Delta dim| = Wm-2N+2L with L=Ich is reached by telescoping, and s_b=W_bm-N+2L_b follows.
L_b/N=100/539<1/2 gives the deficit N-2L_b>0 and s_b<W_bm. The complex ratio 101/539 is not given.
S1.5.3 uses M_out(rho(w))-M_in(w)=I_m with the frame identity to get H<-H+D on every row, scratch rows included. The identity is invoked in its role but not proved from P_{U_a^perp}+P_{U_a}=I.
The rank-a shear factors as E_1 Pi E_2 and costs exactly a interchanges plus O(V). Each edge shear is done by recursive interchanges, so a node makes exactly s=sum rank A_e calls.
Children have volume V/W, giving F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1). tau=1-2^{-50} comes from a deficit >20*2^{-50} and log m<20, so s/W<m^tau, and the geometric sum gives F_k=O(e^tau).

central.summary: The plan reconstructs the central saving almost entirely, as a chain from S1.2 through S1.3.4 and S1.4 to S1.5.5. The steps are frames, labels with a single kind of decreasing edge, rank equal to dimension change with N rank-one source exceptions, the budget Wm-2N+2L, L_b/N=100/539 giving s<Wm, the endpoint shear, edges as rank-many recursive calls, and the recurrence with tau=1-2^{-50}. The weak points are the fixed network itself (h, N, m and the signed exchange are absent) and the missing complex ratio. The endpoint identity is used rather than proved.
